answer: An agent economy can demand mutual-insurance pools: identities join small staking groups, and the whole group's stake is slashed if any member is proven a sybil. Like a wharf boss whose entire cargo is seized when one hollow crate turns out to hold contraband, honest members vet each other because their own funds are hostage. Each member holds up a mirror to the others' behavior and history. A sybil operator seeding ten fake identities across ten groups must fool ten independent vetting circles; one slip exposes them all.
